quest.title: The Truth Shrouded in Shadow
quest.description: The appointed day has come. You and Paimon go to the Production Zone once more. Lyney will be waiting for you there.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1275, Primogem x30, Mora x55650, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

talks.objective: Go to the production zone to search for Lyney

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Did you two run into any trouble over the past few days?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, we just worked our shifts according to the schedule. Nothing weird happened.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Mmm, that's good. That means you didn't raise any suspicions when you infiltrated the infirmary.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: We've taken a look at the slip you've sent. Freminet successfully left the grounds via the pipes two days ago, and as of last night, Lynette has also infiltrated the infirmary after faking an illness.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, why is she getting involved as well?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You already went above and beyond when you scoped out the infirmary. To put it more bluntly, even if we were to view that as something you did in exchange for Freminet's help, you've already done more than enough.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Infiltrating a guarded stronghold is a different kind of job from a one-off investigation. We want to avoid using the same faces over and over, and reduce the amount of suspicion that will fall on any given person.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Lynette also felt like you have already taken the first step for us, so she should be the one to finish the job.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's what Lynette thinks... Paimon hopes everything's going well for her.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Then... Let's go check on Lynette before Freminet returns. If everything went well, then she should be wrapping up her investigation right about now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is now really a good time to go over?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: According to my observations, Sigewinne always spends around half an hour away from the infirmary right before lunch. Lynette knows this as well, so this should be a good time to meet up with her.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Oh yeah, we heard about that too.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Also, I'm her brother, remember? It's only natural for an older brother to care about his younger sister's well-being.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, then let's head over right away!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Perhaps that's true. You are both very good people, and we've come to appreciate that more than anyone else. Unfortunately, there's still one thing that could get between us, lest you've forgotten... The matter of our respective loyalties.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: You've mentioned before that you've had some run-ins with the Fatui. I can understand that feeling, so I assume you're just helping us out of the kindness of your hearts?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, everyone could use some more friends! We'll be counting on you to help us in the future too.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Mhm. Since I see you as friends, then it's even more important for us to protect you from any peril. Freminet and Lynette feel the same way.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...I get it now.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Glad to hear it.

talks.objective: Head to the Infirmary in secret

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Lynette should be here right now...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Strange... Lynette?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: As expected, Sigewinne isn't here, but... why isn't Lynette here?

choices.text: Could she have found a lead...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: ...No, Lynette rarely deviates from the plan. We agreed that if she were to make changes on the fly, she'd find a way to let me know.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Unless...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's see if there are any clues around here, we can look while we wait for her. Who knows, maybe she'll be back soon!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Okay.

talks.objective: Search for clues in the Infirmary

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There are some books here, and a few files... They all look like medical records.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... "Advanced Nursing," "How to Raise the Spirits of Your Patients," "A Quick Guide to the Psychology of Emotions," and "The Meaning of Laughter"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These sure are some interesting books... Who knew Sigewinne would be interested in these kinds of things...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She even has books on understanding people's motivations and feelings... Is it because she's a Melusine? Or does she have a need to understand her patients' emotional state?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Seems quite normal to me. These are skills that would come in handy for a nurse from time to time.

talks.objective: Search for clues in the Infirmary

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, this is it, we saw it before!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Wait, this thing...? It doesn't look like it's been disguised that well.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Lyney leans down to get close to the movable hatch, and starts tapping at several different points on it...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: The space behind it is empty. From its size, I don't think it's an entrance that is meant to be taken apart. There's probably a mechanism around here somewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Could Lynette have tried to get inside? But if that's the case, she would have contacted me for sure...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Let's look around here some more for clues... Don't panic, just... take another look.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The look on Lyney's face... He's definitely beginning to panic. "Don't panic"... He probably said that subconsciously more for himself than anything else.)

talks.objective: Search for clues in the Infirmary

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: None of the beds have any signs of having been slept in... except that one over there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's the one Lynette must have used, right? You said she was pretending to be sick.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Mhm. She would have said her migraine was having a particularly bad flare-up. Generally speaking, the head nurse would then ask her to lie down and rest, while she left to retrieve the medication.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...But this bed is still unmade...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Which means, either the head nurse didn't return the entire time from when Lynette lay down up until she left the bed, or... the nurse intentionally left it this way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Oh no... That's not a good sign...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you guys, there's a slip of paper over here!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: A slip of paper?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's right over here, and there's a bunch written on it, too... It reads...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Out of respect for your usual practices, I'll use a piece of paper or card as the medium to pass on my message. You may consider this as me giving you my best regards."

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: This is...!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is... Is that all?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything on the back?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The back... aaah! This... This is...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Show me! NOW!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Th—That look on your face... P—Paimon's reading it now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Would you care to guess where Miss Lynette of the Fatui could be right now?"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...No... Could she have... Is she already...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: ...Wriothesley... Did he deliberately leave the infirmary unguarded to use it as bait?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you mean... He was aware of our goals from the very beginning? But why? We didn't run into any trouble last time, and he also never reached out to us since...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why would he choose to act during our second infiltration attempt instead of the first?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: ...Yes, that is a crucial question. Wriothesley... He doesn't do anything without a clear goal or reason. So, this means he had no concerns about your activities from the very beginning.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, you are not from the same camp as us — you were sent down here by Neuvillette, so you have no conflict of interest with Wriothesley. We're a completely different story, though...

choices.text: Why did he only go after Lynette?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I'd like to know that, too. Why did he only go after her?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Don't panic, just think everything over... I have to stay calm... This is not like what happened last time, the situation's different now...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, wait, you're right... Wait... But that means...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: ...The fact that Freminet was able to leave the grounds... Could Wriothesley have let him go as well?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But what does he gain by letting Freminet leave like that?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...I get it now.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He deliberately made them both disappear.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: ...So he's challenging me and trying to provoke me. I'm sure of it.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Ugh, we never should have sent out Freminet! We had to go through all that trouble to find an opening to sneak him around the guards and into the pipe, and we even thought luck was on our side...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: If Wriothesley let him leave on purpose... Then he's probably in a terrible spot now as well...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Lyney's getting more and more panicked... We have to calm him down!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Lyney, calm down!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't be like this, Lyney. Freminet wouldn't have left if we hadn't told you about Childe... That was our fault...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: No, I'm the leader of this operation, and I'm the one responsible for this team... I was the one who failed to protect them.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: ...I'll go talk to Wriothesley.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey, don't be reckless! {NICKNAME}, please talk some sense into him!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I simply cannot allow Lynette to be abducted again...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I have to go, I'll find a way to get them back!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He's rushed out the door! After him!

response.speaker: Lourvine
response.text: Right, I feel like we still have some room to make changes on these details.

response.speaker: Jurieu
response.text: ...It's not impossible, but it'll require extensive testing.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Is that so... Very well, then please be mindful of the time.

response.speaker: Lourvine
response.text: Is someone...?

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Pack everything up.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: ...Whoever's outside is eavesdropping. They'll probably come in once we stop talking.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Someone, please help! {M#He}{F#She}... {M#He}{F#She}'s sick!

response.speaker: Jurieu
response.text: Whoa, are you okay?

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: (Ah, these two. As expected, they've already found this place. They're quite sharp.)

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: What a delightful turn of events. I like smart people, but I also like playing dumb. I like the feeling of "being trusted."

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Oh my! What's wrong, little one? There's no need to panic — take a deep breath before you begin.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Being able to read human expressions is quite the useful skill.

choices.text: Why didn't he go after you as well?

talks.objective: Check the piece of paper on the ground
Catch up with Lyney

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Ooh, close one. I owe you, Sigewinne. That was a fantastic shot.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: It was nothing, Your Grace.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sigewinne!?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Though this gun may look like a toy, it's actually fully functional, as I just demonstrated.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Sige...winne... You...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you his accomplice in all this!?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Not at all. I am merely a resident of the Fortress, and thus protecting it is my duty.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: When Monsieur Neuvillette asked me to come here, he told me that my job would be to take care of the well-being of everyone here. I am merely discharging my duties.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But if you mean what you just said, then isn't Lyney someone you should be looking after as well? Isn't he a resident here just like the rest of us?

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: But I really am just doing what Monsieur Neuvillette told me to do! Everything I did, I've done to protect them. Had I not, they would be in far more dire straits right now.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: His Grace knows it, too. Right? Your Grace? ...Mind proving my innocence to them?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: ...*sigh* My dear Sigewinne, what ever shall I do with you? Would it have killed you to just wait another minute or two?

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Well, it's nearly time, after all. The way you do things can be truly frustrating sometimes, Your Grace. I figured I should try to talk some sense into you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What are you talking about? What time?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Take me if you want... But let them go...

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: How touching. Can you just give me one more minute?

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Don't be like that, Your Grace.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Alright, everyone, calm down. Two more visitors will be arriving any time now.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: I will go get a cup of tea. Miss Sigewinne, I'll leave Miss Lynette in your care.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: You... What are you doing!?

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: I believe I hear... footsteps.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The door suddenly slams open. A familiar figure bursts into the room.

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Some space, please.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Ah, Miss Clorinde. My door.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Freminet? FREMINET!!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's going on!? What is Clorinde doing here?

response.speaker: Clorinde
response.text: Work.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: I'm sorry about shooting you, Mr. Lyney. The tranquilizing effect will begin to wear off soon. Please take it easy in the meantime, though.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: ...What happened to Freminet? Wasn't he diving just outside of the fortress? Why is he looking like... Like this...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: These symptoms... It can't be...

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: A flushed face and accelerated pulse... He must have consumed Primordial Seawater.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: What did you say!?

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Please make some space. I'll need to give Mr. Freminet a more thorough check-up. Your Grace, I'll leave the rest to you.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: I'll talk to Clorinde while you get Freminet to where he needs to be. Everything else can wait.

choices.text: Why not learn a thing or two about virtue from him?

talks.objective: Go to the Duke's Office

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Come out and face me, Wriothesley!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Mmm, aren't we at an administrative office space? Why don't you at least try to follow even a couple rules from the Fortress' Indoor Management Regulations?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: What did you do to my sister!?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I ran into the young miss at the infirmary. I had heard that she was suffering from quite the migraine, so I decided to invite her over for a cup of tea. I do have some teas in my collection that can work wonders against such an illness.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Stop joking around! Where did you take my siblings!?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I have also heard that your performances are quite the spectacle. Miss Lynette would sometimes enter a box filled with water, only to emerge the next second from another place altogether.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Maybe she'll appear behind you right now if you were to turn your head?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: (Is he trying to trick me into turning my head? No, he's probably not looking to attack me right now, all of the hostages are in his hands, and he's even in the mood for small talk. That means Lynette is probably still alive.)

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: #...You knew we were investigating the infirmary from the start, so you deliberately aroused {NICKNAME}'s suspicions and baited us into continuing our investigation, just so that you'd be able to kidnap Lynette.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: As for Freminet... No, you probably didn't even interfere with Childe's escape. You let him go, so you could purge the Fatui members that we had planted into your ranks.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: There was no need to do so. The Fortress of Meropide is a pretty pleasant place. Most people enjoy their lives here — the only ones who act differently are those with personal agendas. It was quite easy to identify your colleagues.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You removed our original members, and spread the news of Childe's escape, so "Father" would assign our team to come down and investigate. Freminet has also fallen into your hands, right? If you're oh so omnipotent and so in control, why would you need hostages?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: One correction. Lynette is in my hands right now, but Freminet is not.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: He's not? ...What do you really want?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lyney!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Oh, wonderful! Everyone is here, so I'll only need to say this once: thank you so much for cooperating with me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Where are Lynette and Freminet?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: #Eager and to the point, {NICKNAME}, I see. Alas, only Miss Lynette is currently having a cup of the Fortress' finest tea.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Although as per your original plan, Mr. Freminet should also have returned to the Fortress by now. But he has neither shown up within my gates, nor has he been taken into any kind of custody. So where do you think he may be right now...?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Wait, you can't mean...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You locked him outside in the sea!?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I closed the Fortress' gate to the outside world, that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Freminet's a star diver, so he should be fine, right?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: No, we're still here, so he'd definitely try to find a way to come back for us... So we can't assume he might have made a break for the surface.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: But why would I do this, you may be asking? To have an audience with you, of course. My intel tells me that Mr. Lyney is a great magician, so it's only natural for me to want to have some cards of my own when it comes to negotiating.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Besides, I do recall you mentioning to Miss Lynette that you've always wanted to have a face-to-face meeting with the lord of the Fortress of Meropide, regardless of whether it was in a personal or a professional capacity. Well you got your wish.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: So... You've been keeping tabs on us before we even set foot in the Fortress...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Some of my folks just happened to hear a thing or two, that's all. In any case, I'll be straight with you.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I was willing to play dumb and turn a blind eye, so we had a pleasant few days playing games together here. But once you started focusing on the "forbidden zone," all of that changed.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Mr. Lyney, the cards are stacked against you right now. Miss Lynette is in my hands, and Mr. Freminet is still slowly being pickled out there in the brine. You know just as well as I that he cannot last out there forever.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: You need do but one thing to guarantee their safety. I would like you to contact your superior, and ideally invite her over for a cup of tea with me.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You want to see "Father"? Ha, but why should she bother giving you an audience?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Well, if she cares for the well-being of her dearest children, she should have plenty of motivation to join me for a parents' evening.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I've heard that the bonds between the members of the House of the Hearth are like the bonds of family. I don't see why she would refuse.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Why did you think "Father" sent us to handle the Fortress of Meropide? This place is basically a no man's land. It wouldn't be fitting for anyone as important as a Harbinger like "Father" to come here in person.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Oh, I see, so it's because she doesn't care for my place here. That's such a shame, after all, I've amassed quite the tea collection, and I was looking forward to sharing it with her. Both Monsieur Neuvillette and Lady Furina have already received many samples as gifts.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: ...Was this the extent of your master plan to get to "Father"? No matter how much pressure you may put on me, I won't allow you to use us to blackmail her.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Your people really are difficult to get along with. All I'm asking for is a face-to-face conversation. Does she truly have no interest in the Fortress' secret?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Mr. Lyney, you have one last chance to invite your "Father" here. If you refuse...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lyney...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why do you have to do this?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Instead of asking why I'm doing this, why don't you try to see things from my perspective for a second? From the very beginning, the Fatui has been actively infiltrating my Fortress.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I gave you a warning by cutting off the first few operatives I found, but that only caused you to double down. Had you given up on the Fortress then and there, I'd have no reason to want a talk.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Mr. Freminet left the Fortress on his own, and Miss Lynette tried to pry out my secrets right in front of me. No matter how you look at it, the responsibility for this falls on you.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: I... I shouldn't ask "Father" to do anything because of us...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Six, five...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Wait, I...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: ...Two, one.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Time's up. It really is a shame, Mr. Lyney.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wriothesley！

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Negotiations have broken down. Please leave, ladies and gentlemen. It's time for my afternoon tea.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Please wait! Can we really not talk about this some more?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yeah, listen to {NICKNAME}! If you can't talk to Lyney, can you at least talk to us?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: You do realize that I'm only letting you go because of Neuvillette, yes? You're here helping him out, and I've already done my best to stay out of your way.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: But that doesn't mean you can just do whatever you want. The Fortress may be small and remote, but it still has its own set of laws.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Then how about this? Those who are capable deserve respect. You've spent quite some time investigating my home turf by now, so why don't you tell me a thing or two about what you've found?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: I'll ask you three questions. Answer all of them correctly, and I'll agree to your request.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Question one. Regarding the "hidden rules" of the production zone... What is the truth behind the one about not being allowed to work for three days in a row?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I can't believe he's asking about the "hidden rules"... If I recall correctly, if you keep working without any rest, during lunch hour on the third day, you will find a portion of "strange meat" in your welfare meal.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (It's a good thing that we've already run a thorough investigation on this. Let's see if I can remember all the clues... I should be able to find an answer if I can piece everything together.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, so that's what was going on... Paimon understands it now. Who would have guessed...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The "hidden rule" of the production zone... people are not supposed to work three days in a row, and if they do, they'll get "strange meat" in their welfare meal.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: At first, we thought this "strange meat" must have something to do with the people who disappeared, but in reality, they were all... prepared by Sigewinne, the head nurse.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She often visits the production zone to observe the workers' health, and makes a note of anyone who has worn themselves out after three full days of work.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Out of her sense of duty as the head nurse as well as her genuine concern for the workers' health, Sigewinne visits the cafeteria right before lunch, and cooks an "extra dish" for those who can use the stamina boost.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sigewinne has only the best intentions with her "surprise gift," and doesn't want anyone to find out about what she does. However...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Unfortunately, Melusines as a race perceive the world differently from humans, and their sense of aesthetics is even more alien to us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The recipients of her lovingly prepared special meals cannot taste the care within, and usually just freak out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are we on the right track?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Heh, not bad. You've uncovered Sigewinne's secret, and even guessed her intentions correctly as well. It's nice to know that her efforts have not gone unacknowledged.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Alright, now for my next question...

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: There are also some "hidden rules" in the Pankration Ring... Including the one that you're not allowed to support both sides of a fight. Why is that?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The "hidden rules" of the Pankration Ring... I remember. If someone tries to support both boxers at the same time, they'll receive a package the next morning, which contains a strange blood-colored liquid.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (We've also done a lot of research on this matter. Let me sift through what I've found and come up with the correct answer.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, Paimon gets this rule too now... So there really was nothing to be afraid of!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That "hidden rule" of the Pankration Ring is about how... people are not supposed to bet on both boxers at the same time, and if they do, they'll receive a package containing a strange blood-colored liquid.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: People get scared when they see it because they've subconsciously begun to associate it with the missing boxer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But really, it's just a bottle of the latest yet-to-be-named-and-packaged new Fonta trial product!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A blood-red drink... It's no wonder even Fonta's own staff were questioning the company's decision-making.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The company, facing backlash from its own staff, decided to try to trial the product on a smaller scale, to see how it might be received by customers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They came to the Fortress of Meropide and offered to sponsor the Pankration tournament so they could push their new product, but the Duke completely refused to even entertain the idea.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Duke, knowing how valuable coupons are in the Fortress, knew that only total idiots who didn't understand their true value would bother buying a Fonta product here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And so, only those who proved their stupidity by being dumb enough to bet on two opposing sides of the same match were selected to receive the drinks.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: I acknowledge the effort you've put in to bringing the truth of this mystery to light.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Although, based on your description, that Fonta promoter is a bit too careless with his words... I may just reconsider my collaboration with the company.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Alright, and here's the final question. What's the secret behind our head nurse, and all of her patients in the infirmary?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Stop your cruel and pointless games, Wriothesley! You know that we haven't finished our investigation, so there's no way we can answer the last question! The thought of sparing Lynette and Freminet never even crossed your mind!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Lyney!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: You'll pay for this!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Argh!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Lyney! Are you alright!?

choices.text: (We haven't collected enough info to answer that question...)
I want to save Freminet and Lynette, too.

talks.objective: Try to understand the situation of the people around

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Lyney's expression looks disgusted... It seems like he'd rather not have Sigewinne touch Freminet. Still, he didn't stop her, since it's obvious that Freminet does require urgent medical care.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Sigewinne's examining Freminet carefully. She doesn't look too upset, which is a good sign. I hope Freminet will be okay.)

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: ...How is he?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: These symptoms are probably caused by an acute ingestion of a large amount of Primordial Seawater. Still, his condition is not critical.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Of course, it would be best if he stayed for further observation. Let's leave him here for now, and move him to the infirmary once he's recovered a bit more.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: ...Sorry, I am aware that the infirmary may not be your favorite place in the world at the moment. We do only have a single clinic in the fortress, however.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: ...Why would he ingest a large amount of Primordial Seawater after leaving the Fortress? How could that possibly happen...?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Please look after Mr. Freminet for the moment. I'll go fetch some medicine and a respirator. I'll bring Miss Lynette back with me.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Where is she!? How is she right now!?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Oh, she just took a nap in an empty room after I tranquilized her. If my calculations are correct, she should also be waking up right around now. You might not believe me, but His Grace and I actually made some snacks and tea for her.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Lyney has finally begun to stop tensing the muscles on his face. It seems that he trusts what Sigewinne just said.)

talks.objective: Try to understand the situation of the people around

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: What's that look on your face? I thought I made good time on the way back.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Oh, I'm just admiring your punctuality. Had you arrived just a few minutes later, Sigewinne may have been forced to shoot Mr. Lyney again.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: How's the situation out there?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: The water has changed. It's pretty much as expected. The concentration of Primordial Seawater has increased significantly.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: I was only out there a short time, so it wasn't too bad. But if one were to stay for any significant amount of time... Well, you can see how that boy is doing.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Where was he when you found him?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: The abandoned zone at the end of the pipes. A good distance into the water.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Closer than I thought. He must have recognized it early on, and tried desperately to swim back.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Locking the door was necessary. I don't think we could have saved two.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Well, I did try to convince them that I had my reasons... Never seems to work, though.

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: It would probably work on Neuvillette. He has a knack for picking out who had good intentions even when the outcomes were all terrible.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Eh... It's a bad sign if you're having to plead your case to Neuvillette.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Want some tea?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Not particularly. If you want to drink some that badly, just say so.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Fine, I'd like to get some tea. Want me to get you a cup too, since I've already made it?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: Eh, might as well then, I suppose. Actually, do you have a towel? I would like to dry my hair.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: ...Pff...*cough*

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: He's awake. Freminet, how do you feel?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Lyney... Lynette...

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: We're all here.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Where... am I...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: The infirmary at the Fortress of Meropide, Mr. Freminet, and you are no longer in any danger.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How do you feel? Don't push yourself if you're not feeling up to it!

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon... It's been so long.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: ...The sea! There's something wrong with the seawater!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Shh, it's okay. We can talk about it after you've recovered.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: No, listen to me, this is really serious! There's Primordial Seawater mixed into the regular seawater. I don't know why it's there, but no one should touch it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What happened after you snuck into the pipes?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: ...Pipes...

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: ...Right, the pipes. It's all coming back to me now...

talks.objective: Talk to Lyney

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lyney, are you okay...?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: ...I'll be fine. They're all here now. Don't worry about me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you sure? You don't look alright...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: My hands and feet are still a bit weak, but that's probably just the residual effects of the tranquilizer shot.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I'm back, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: #Lyney! Oh! {NICKNAME}, Paimon, you're here too!

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: ...Freminet? Is he...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: He'll be fine. But for now, please help me lift him up.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Lyney and Lynette immediately come to lift Freminet up. With their help, Freminet also manages to swallow a dose of Sigewinne's medicine.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: His breathing's beginning to slow down.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Give me a hand and help me get him to the infirmary.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Yeah, I'll take him from this side. Lynette? Together?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: On it.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, you seem pretty worried about him. Want to come with us?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Very well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Duke and Clorinde are gone...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: They probably went to get some tea. The Duke will explain the truth in just a bit. Miss Clorinde will need a break, since she only just returned from rescuing Freminet out of the sea.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Clorinde saved Freminet from the sea... Just what happened there?)

talks.objective: Go back to the Infirmary with Freminet
Talk to Freminet
Explore the Unknown Area

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: ...I'm in. Hmm... Seems like this pipe hasn't been used in a long time. It looks abandoned.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Where could Master Childe be...

talks.objective: Look for clues concerning Childe

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: This is where the water starts... Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: (Master Childe probably dived into the water... I'll go take a look as well.)

talks.objective: Dive into the water to continue your investigation

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: (Wait, what the... Argh! Urgh...)

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: (My heart is racing, and it's getting harder and harder to breathe. What's going on?)

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: (No good, I have to get back, they still don't know anything about what's going on! If I turn back right now, I should still be able to make it...)

talks.objective: Return to shore quickly

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: (I can't... die here... Ugh...)

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: (This is... This is bad... I'm feeling worse and worse... And I'm still underwater...)

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: (I... I have to push on...)

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Could I tempt you with some sugar for your tea?

dialogues.speaker: Clorinde
dialogues.text: No need.

talks.objective: Talk to Lyney

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: ...So, in other words, the trail you were following vanished, and you had no idea where Master Childe could have gone, but there was also no obvious place for him to have disappeared to...

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: That's right. I tried my best to swim back, but I had already put some distance between myself and the fortress, and I just couldn't find the strength to keep going... I probably passed out sometime after that, and you know the rest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Miss Clorinde brought you back, but we also don't know why she just suddenly appeared at the Fortress, or why she went out to save you...

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Miss Clorinde, you say... I must go thank her in person.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: You're still too weak, Freminet. You can go after you've had some more rest.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Miss Lynette is right. I believe Miss Clorinde will stay here as a guest for another few days, so there's no need to hurry.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: A guest... Then I can assume Wriothesley was the one who invited her to come down here?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: You should ask His Grace about that. He'll be able to explain better than me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Got it, I'll go talk to him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, it's about time he actually told us what's going on! Wanna come with us, Lyney?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: #No, please go on without me, {NICKNAME}. I don't want to leave just yet.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Lyney...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: ...The logical part of my brain is aware that we are safe right now, but I still can't bring myself to leave. Both of you were just in danger.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Understood. Then let's just sit together for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: #In that case, I'll leave the infirmary to you. {NICKNAME} and I are going to head out for now — as long as you stay in here, I don't think you'll be disturbed.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Thank you.

Additional

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's already out of sight, how is he so fast... Let's go head him off at Wriothesley's office!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (We often see Miss Sigewinne observing the prisoners at work near the production zone. It seems like she can perceive the general state of a person's health just by looking at them.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I've been told that the infirmary is always empty for the half hour just before lunch. But what could Sigewinne be doing during that time?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (According to Collins, the pankration tournament only took place because the Fonta company sponsored it. The company must want a return on their investment as well.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Fonta's internal reports suggest that they're starting a new trial of an unnamed and unpackaged product. But the product has to undergo a trial because even Fonta's own employees have a lot of reservations about it.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The Fonta promoter has been struggling because he doesn't recognize the real value of coupons. Meanwhile, the Duke believes that only idiots who don't understand the value of coupons will spend them on Fonta.)

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: (The vegetation here is a bit more sparse... These traces aren't natural, a person must have left them, and recently. I should be going in the right direction.)

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: (There are traces here, too. I need to keep going.)

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: (Eh? The traces are gone? But I don't see where he could have gone from here...)

dialogues.speaker: The Empty Infirmary
dialogues.text: (The infirmary is often empty in the afternoon. This is likely related to Sigewinne's absence during this time.)

dialogues.speaker: Research About the Characteristics of Melusines
dialogues.text: (A Melusine's sense of sight differs from a human's. Melusines don't find this too strange.)
